headline: No budget moves this week: LinkedIn CPA is up but sits above the 1.5 ROAS target under 4 of 5 attribution models, so I'm testing it rather than cutting.

tests.hypothesis: LinkedIn's true incremental ROAS is at or above the 1.5 target (models range 1.13 to 2.11), so the recent CPA rise is noise or a mild decline, not waste.
tests.design: Geo holdout: pause LinkedIn in about 30% of matched regions (or audience holdout) for 4 weeks. Measure total conversions and revenue in held-out vs exposed regions, including untracked/direct and self-reported 'LinkedIn' answers. Decision rule: if incremental ROAS is below 1.5, cut the budget by at least 50%.

flag_verdicts.reason: LinkedIn CPA rose from $156 to $238 (1.52x) after 2026-10-18. The 3-week trend view shows a smaller rise, $159 to $189 (+18%), under the 40% trim threshold. Weekly conversions are 7-20, so the series is noisy. Implied ROAS is 2.11 (first-touch), 2.11 (Markov), 1.78 (linear) and 1.60 (time-decay), all above the 1.5 target. Only last-touch (1.13) is below it. That rules out a cut, so I'm recommending a holdout test.

flags.message: linkedin CPA rose 1.5x, from $156 to $238, starting 2026-10-18.
